issues.description: data.sh overwrites utt.list mid-pipeline, hiding a silent filter step
issues.detail: In local/data.sh, utt.list is first written from wav.flist, then rewritten from transcripts.txt after filter_scp.pl. The second write silently shadows the first and is never used downstream. State the invariant: 'utt.list = set of utterances that survive transcript filtering' — or delete the second write. As written, a reader cannot tell which utt.list is authoritative.

issues.description: Transcript join uses sort -u without a sorted-key invariant, risking misaligned text
issues.detail: The paste joins sort -u on utt_uttid (column 1 = utt) with sort -u on transcripts.txt (column 1 = utt). These align only if both files have identical utterance sets after filtering. No assertion verifies this; if filter_scp.pl drops any line, the paste silently produces mismatched (uttid, text) pairs. Use join -1 1 -2 1 or add a count-equality check before paste.

issues.description: download_and_untar.sh does not exit when unzip is missing
issues.detail: The unzip-missing branch only echoes a message and falls through, then the script attempts unzip anyway and dies with an opaque error. Either exit 1 in the guard, or remove the guard. The current form is the worst of both worlds: it pretends to check, then doesn't act on the check.

issues.description: README links to a non-existent config path
issues.detail: README references ./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml but the actual file is conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml (no train/ subdir). A reader following the link will hit 404. Either move the file or fix the link; pick one and make the documentation match the tree.

issues.description: Hardcoded utterance counts encode a fragile invariant without explanation
issues.detail: Heredoc lists exact counts (22467, 3208, 6072, 29386, 38924) checked against wc -l of text. The invariant 'these numbers come from the published TAL split' should be stated as a comment, with a citation to the dataset version. Otherwise a future dataset re-release silently fails the check with no clue why these specific numbers were chosen.

issues.description: Inline sed character-substitution chain lacks a stated normalization rule
issues.detail: The text-normalization sed chain strips Ａ→A, '#', '=', '、', '，', '？', '。', trailing spaces. No comment states the normalization policy or why these specific punctuation marks. A literate comment ('CER scoring excludes punctuation; full-width A normalized to ASCII to match LM vocab') would let the next maintainer extend the list without guessing.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The recipe is structurally typical for an ESPnet egs2 contribution and the reported CER numbers are plausible, but the data-preparation shell script has two real correctness hazards: utt.list is written twice with different semantics, and the transcripts-to-uttid join uses paste over sort -u rather than a keyed join, so any filtering asymmetry produces silent misalignment between audio and text. The download script has a dead unzip-missing guard, and the README links to a config path that does not exist. None of these block running the recipe on the exact dataset the author used, but they will bite the next person who tries to reproduce or extend it. Add stated invariants, replace paste with join, and fix the README link before merge.
